memory_candidates.content: When a plan's own verification criterion is a literal grep for a now-eliminated syntactic device (e.g. `grep -n 'clause (a)' <target>` must return zero hits), a later phase that must still DESCRIBE the elimination in historical/ledger prose (an amendment note, a decision record, an evidence-tier table row) will collide with that criterion if it uses the exact literal substring, even though the surrounding prose correctly marks the device as superseded. Resolve by using a lightly respelled form (e.g. hyphenating 'clause (a)' to 'clause-(a)') that preserves readability while falling outside the grep's exact-match scope. Re-run the grep after any such historical-prose edit, not just after the structural edits, since this class of collision is easy to introduce in exactly the paragraphs that are SUPPOSED to talk about the eliminated thing.
